appearance_facts.fact: Four stacked bars are aligned to the x-axis labels May 09, May 08, May 06, and May 07 from left to right.
The blue Station X segment is a thin base at the bottom of the stack, with the green Station Y segment directly above it and the orange Station Z segment forming the top.
The blue Station X segment is visibly thicker than the May 06 blue segment, extending from the 1,500 baseline to roughly the 1,750–1,800 level.
No visible blue Station X segment appears at the base; the green Station Y segment starts at the 1,500 baseline.
Legend swatches are ordered blue = Station X, green = Station Y, orange = Station Z.

printed_facts.fact: “Visitors at Three Train Stations in City Z”
Axis label “Number of Visitors”; ticks printed at 1,500, 2,000, 2,500, 3,000, 3,500, 4,000, 4,500, 5,000.
Review target is “Station X on May 06”; operations program is “Demand status routing”.

public_definitions: Choose the May 06 Station X demand route from: “Keep May 06 on normal Station X demand monitoring”, “Route May 06 to low-demand response”, or “Route May 06 to high-demand crowding response”.
The transit dashboard is the evidence source for the May 06 Station X routing decision.
uncertain: No printed threshold defines what visitor count qualifies as normal, low-demand, or high-demand crowding.
The exact numeric value of the May 06 Station X segment is not printed; it must be read from the stacked-bar height.
No policy table is provided to map a specific visitor count to a routing option.
